newsitem.title: USA: US legislation aims to close corp. tax loophole.
newsitem.headline: US legislation aims to close corp. tax loophole.

text.p: Legislation was introduced in the House of Representatives and Senate Thursday aimed at closing a loophole that can allow corporations to spin-off subsidiaries without paying taxes, lawmakers said.
Identical legislation was introduced in the House and Senate by the chairmen of the committees that deal with taxes.
The legislation aims to prevent corporations from avoiding paying taxes by undertaking complicated transactions when they spin-off subsidiaries, the lawmakers said.
If enacted, the legislation would be effective as of April 16, 1997.
"Congress did not intend that section 355 (of the Internal Revenue Code) apply to insulate these transactions from tax," a statement from the sponsors of the legislation said.

"Section 355 was intended to permit tax-free restructurings of several businesses among existing shareholders, with limitations to prevent the bail-out of corporate earnings and profits to the shareholders as capital gains," the statement said.

The sponsors of the legislation were House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, a Texas Republican, and Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth, a Delaware Republican, along with the ranking Democrat on the Finance Committee, Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan of New York.

The legislation would modify the tax treatment of "certain pre-arranged corporate sale transactions which might otherwise be characterized as tax-free spinoffs," the House Ways and Means Committee said.
